item.title: Can Tadej Pogačar win all three Grand Tours in a season?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: original reporting, evidence and concrete detail

The question for five-time Tour de France winner Tadej Pogačar came from Tuttobiciweb during a friendly round of media interviews at an annual padel tournament put on by his agent, Alex Carera. Eddy Merckx, the greatest men's road racer of all time, had suggested in a separate interview back home in Belgium that perhaps Pogačar could win all three of cycling's Grand Tours – the Giro d'Italia, Tour de France and Vuelta a España – in a single season.

The feat has never been accomplished, not by Merckx or any other man. So what did Pogačar think of an attempt? "I don't rule it out; in fact, I'll try it sooner or later," he replied. There are certain caveats to raise here. It's possible he was just engaging in some friendly banter and has no serious intention of making an attempt. It's possible he's loosely entertaining the possibility and will change his mind.

But as responses go, it's a step further than his answer the last time he spoke about it, roughly a year ago in a Sky Sports interview. When the question arose then, "I don't know if I would do it," he hedged, saying he'd need to discuss it with team management, in particular because it would prevent other talented riders on his UAE Team Emirates-XRG squad from targeting their own objectives. "I don't think it's fair if I claim all the big Tours," he said.

Now, apparently, it's sooner or later. But likely not sooner, and it's certainly not a slam dunk. Even for the greatest racer in several generations, and perhaps ever, there are a ton of obstacles that stand in the way. Why hasn't anyone ever accomplished the feat, and what needs to happen for Pogačar to be the one to do it?

Wait, no one's ever won all three in a season?

New Zealand vs India: Tom Latham laughs off Rishabh Pant dominating local Christchurch cricket match under false name

Footage emerged this week of India's Rishabh Pant scoring 54 off 21 balls for local Christchurch cricket club Open House Swingers under false name 'Stan Stan'; Pant played one day before second New Zealand vs India Test begins; Black Caps captain Tom Latham laughs it off as 'brilliant'

Thursday 26 November 2026 21:06, UK

New Zealand captain Tom Latham has laughed off India's Rishabh Pant dominating a local Christchurch cricket match under a false name, a day before their second Test.

On Monday, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips held firm for 43 overs to earn the Black Caps a hard-fought draw in Wellington after India posted a record score of 720-9d.

Pant scored 128 in that Test, with the second Test between the sides beginning on Thursday at Hagley Oval.

Yet, footage has since emerged of Pant playing for club side Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones on Wednesday, scoring 54 off 21 balls under the name 'Stan Stan' to seal a 16-run victory.

In an interview with The New Zealand Herald, Open House player Mohammad Safi said he had seen Pant on an electric bike in the city and asked if he would play, due to his club team being a player short.

"Did he play?! How'd he go?" Latham said at his New Zealand press conference. "That's brilliant!

"It's great. He's obviously a real character of the game, is Rishabh.

"It's great for him to be giving his experience back to LMS (Last Man Standing) teams!"

Pant has scored 3,853 runs in his 53 Tests for India, averaging just below of 45.

The 29-year-old also boasts a strike-rate of 74.43, which is bettered only by Virender Sehwag and Kapil Dev among players to have scored more than 2,000 Test runs for India.

Thursday 26 November 2026 20:05, UK

Bournemouth continued their magnificent run of form with a 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo, creating two bits of history in the process.

It was a club-record-extending 10th successive win for Bournemouth in all competitions, with the victory also marking the first time an English club have won their first five matches in major European competition.

Veteran former Liverpool striker Iago Aspas put the home side in front in style in the first half, before Bournemouth were reduced to 10 men when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a late challenge.

But Alvaro Rodriguez equalised early in the second half, with substitute Rayan coming on to score a late winner to give Bournemouth an unlikely win.

Bournemouth were fortunate not to go behind after 10 minutes, with an offside flag chalking off Pablo Duran's poke home from close-range.

But the Cherries fell behind 10 minutes later when record Celta Vigo goalscorer Aspas scored a screamer.

The 39-year-old had seen an overhead kick saved well by Michele Di Gregorio, but he picked up the ball on the right side of the area in the second phase of play, before cutting inside to curl past the goalkeeper and into the far corner off the post.

Things went from bad to worse for Bournemouth moment later when Diakite saw a yellow card upgraded to a red after a VAR check following a late challenge on Couhaib Driouech.

Tyler Adams replaced Justin Kluivert at half-time and the tactical switch drew an instant reward when Alvaro Rodriguez glanced home Amine Adli's cross to get Bournemouth back on level terms.

James Hill then drew a fine save from Ionut Radu - who is the only player ever to play for both clubs - before Di Gregorio was called into action at the other end to divert a long-range Aspas strike away.

But three Bournemouth substitutes combined for a late winner.

Adrien Truffert stole possession and broke before finding Marcus Tavernier the area. He laid the ball off for Rayan to sweep home and seal victory as Marco Rose's side made more history with a brilliant win at the Estadio Abanca-Balaidos.

item.description:

Why it is here: original reporting, concrete detail

Boxing chiefs to assess Fury mental health before fight

The British Boxing Board of Control is looking into Tyson Fury's comments about his schizophrenia diagnosis but is "fairly confident" the British heavyweight will be cleared to fight Anthony Joshua next month.

Fury, 38, is due to face Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, with the ringwalk expected in the early hours of 12 December.

In a Netflix documentary out on Friday, he says he heard voices threatening him and his family in the months after he beat Wladimir Klitschko to become world champion in 2015.

"We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody," Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told BBC Sport.

"I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly."

Under regulation 8.1(b) of the British Boxing Board of Control's 2026 rules and regulations, external, schizophrenia is among the conditions that "may preclude" a boxer from obtaining a first licence, while for an existing licence holder the board "may take such action as in its absolute discretion it sees fit".

Smith would not say what the process would involve over the next few days, saying "it's a medical matter".

He said that all boxers on the card will undergo medical checks, adding: "If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box."

In the documentary, Fury and his wife Paris recall his admission to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack.

Doctors said he had suffered an anxiety attack. He was diagnosed with schizophrenia after he left hospital, according to the film.

The NHS describes schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury says.

The heavyweight, who struggled with drug and alcohol addiction after beating Klitschko, says a Halloween night out in 2017 prompted him to return to training, calling that a "turning point" after being "embarrassed by how I looked".

He went on to beat Deontay Wilder in 2020 to become world heavyweight champion for a second time.

item.description:

Why it is here: original reporting, concrete detail

Aaron Rodgers: Quarterback 'losing respect' as NFL reacts to stunning Mike McCarthy claims

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claims that head coach Mike McCarthy was 'snoring' in a quarterback meeting in an explosive interview; Steelers president Art Rooney II comes out in "100 per cent" support of McCarthy after team releases Rodgers in light of comments

Thursday 26 November 2026 20:12, UK

Has Aaron Rodgers played his final game in the NFL? Was he wrong to publicly criticise Mike McCarthy? The four-time MVP quarterback is 'losing respect' following his explosive claims about the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach, according to Sky Sports NFL's Jason Bell.

Rodgers sent shockwaves through the NFL on Thanksgiving Eve as he used an interview on The Pat McAfee Show to claim McCarthy had been "falling asleep in meetings" while suggesting his entire team believed a change was required on the sideline.

It came after Rodgers was benched for Friday's matchup with the Denver Broncos following two straight defeats, with Mason Rudolph due to start under center.

The Steelers later released Rodgers 11 weeks into what is set to be the final season of the 42-year-old's career.

- How to watch NFL Thanksgiving week live on Sky Sports

- Jay-Z picks himself to headline Super Bowl half-time show

- Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW

"First of all, I don't want to be on Aaron Rodgers' bad side. Let's start there. We all make mistakes, right? We all do things that aren't necessarily right in the moment," said Sky Sports NFL's Bell.

"But when I look at him as a player, he wasn't playing well. He wasn't helping his team.

"And you could could see him and his head coach arguing on the sideline with with each other. They weren't getting along.

"Whatever happens behind closed doors, that goes down, but the response to it is where I'm losing a little respect.

"In that locker room is a sanctuary. Some things we just don't let out. We don't have those conversations in public - it's a respect thing.

"If Rodgers was playing MVP football like he did before, he could say all these things and get away with it, but you have to know where you are in your career."

Rodgers suggested in his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show that the prospect of being benched had never been mentioned during recent conversations with McCarthy.

He accused McCarthy of snoring during meetings and rebuffing Rodgers' suggestions that he needed to make more of an effort of connecting with the Steelers' defensive players.

Rodgers added that the "final straw" came during half-time of a game when McCarthy closed a team talk by shouting 'one, two, three, Packers!'.

Rodgers and McCarthy spent 13 seasons together with the Packers from 2006-2018, reaching the playoffs nine times and winning one Super Bowl. They were reunited this past offseason when the Steelers hired McCarthy following the departure of Mike Tomlin.

"I'm not sure what's next for Aaron Rodgers. I think he will figure out that for himself over the next handful of months, or whatever his particular process is," said Super Bowl champion and Sky Sports NFL expert Ndamukong Suh.

"But I want to go back to what Jason [Bell] said in the way that you handle your business, especially from the perspective of a star. There's a way you go about handling things.

"Those things should be handled behind closed doors before trying to get ahead of the story - on either side. Have a conversation, have an understanding, and then go from there and address it.

"Going out to the media and doing all of these different things, The Pat McAfee Show, it's great for them and great for ESPN, but it's not the proper way I would want to handle that particular scenario."

Responding to Rodgers' comments, McCarthy admitted to his "embarrassing" moment when mentioning the Packers during half-time of their defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11.

Steelers president gives McCarthy his "100 per cent" backing

Steelers president Art Rooney II defended McCarthy on Thursday in an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, insisting he supports him "100 per cent".

"I just want to say that I have 100 per cent confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Mr Rooney II told the Post-Gazette.

"The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that. There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload.

"He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."

Rooney II underlined his belief that events in the locker room should be kept within the locker room, and downplayed Rodgers' comments regarding concerns for McCarthy's health.

The Steelers are 6-4 as they prepare to face the Denver Broncos (8-2) on Black Friday.

Referee being 'drunk' claims are 'entirely unfounded'

Claims that a referee was drunk during an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match are "entirely unfounded", officials say.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time of the match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates.

Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following what has been described as some erratic decision-making in the first half.

Iranian news agency ISNA quoted one club official as saying: "The referee was not in a normal state," and suggesting they would not have played on had the referee not been removed.

Accusations of drunkenness were also widely shared on social media.

But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has released a statement denying the allegation, saying he has been defamed and threatening legal action.

The fourth official took over for the second half, with Al Jazira winning the match.

Hattab said he will be "issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened".

Omani sports journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian competitions, claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus".

"He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating."

In their statement on the match, which was played in Asia's second tier continental competition, the Syrian Football Association backed Hattab.

"Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media - that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded," they wrote.

"The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident."

item.title: Alexandersson 'overwhelmed' by Swansea interest
item.description:

Why it is here: original reporting, concrete detail

Alexandersson 'overwhelmed' by Swansea interest

Rosenborg head coach Freyr Alexandersson admits he has found it "overwhelming" to be courted by managerless Swansea City and confirmed he has spoken to the Championship side.

Ashley Williams is currently interim boss at the Welsh club as they search for a permanent replacement for Vitor Matos following his shock departure to manage French side Strasbourg.

Icelander Alexandersson, 44, has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June but has already emerged as the front-runner for the Swansea job.

The Norwegian top-flight club were in danger of relegation when he was appointed, but are fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December.

"I can confirm that there is strong interest from Swansea," Alexandersson told Norsk rikskringkasting AS ahead of Saturday's crucial match against Molde, who are just one place behind Rosenborg in the Eliteserien table.

"I have heard from them (Swansea). I've never been in this situation before. Even just that is a bit overwhelming. I have strong emotions towards Rosenborg and particularly the players and the staff that I am working with, so that part is a bit difficult.

"But the interest itself from a club in England [sic] which I have said before, it is my dream to be a coach in English football.

"That in itself is something I find a bit interesting.

"I have no other plans than that I will be standing here tomorrow and hold training, have meetings and preparations ahead of Saturday's match, and be standing at the match on Saturday.

"That is what I can say now, because what has happened has happened very fast. And the last 24 hours I have only had focus on Rosenborg. I have had talks with (Rosenborg sporting director Alfred) Finnbogason, so I am only focusing on Saturday's match."

Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge.

While Alexandersson admits he is unsure whether Swansea have made an official approach to Rosenborg for him, he did confirm he had spoken to the Welsh club.

When asked if he had been offered the Swansea job, Alexandersson replied: "Well, I cannot comment on that because Rosenborg and Swansea... I don't think there are negotiations even, I don't know what Alfred is saying about it, so I cannot comment.

It is them who have come to me and that is of course a great honour to be the one they are hunting for. It is both ways.

Maybe if I have time this evening I will talk with them."
